messages.subject: Problems plotting projected spherical data
parts:
Dear INLA-Group, 

I have some issues plotting projected  data. I am working with spherical data, which has exactly the same format as the CMBData which one can download via downloadCMBMap(). I am not using the full spherical map but slice little windows for analyzing the data. Here is the code and problem description. 

## slicing a window from the sphere which is in Healpix format:

require(„rcosmo“)


## Download SMICA with \code{nside = 2048}

## and save in working directory

## as "CMB_map_smica2048.fits"

downloadCMBMap(foreground = "smica", nside = 2048)


## Load the downloaded map into a CMBDataFrame

sky <- CMBDataFrame("CMB_map_smica2048.fits")


## get sky with cartesian coordinates

cartesian <- CMBDataFrame(sky, coords = "cartesian", ordering = "nested")


## SLICE WINDOW FROM SKY

win_sel <- CMBWindow(theta = c(pi/2.05,pi/2,pi/2,pi/2.05), phi = c(pi/2.05,pi/2.05,pi/2,pi/2))

wind <- window(cartesian, new.window = win_sel)


##save coordinates and data from window in dataframe and matrix

loc.cartesian <- as.matrix(wind[,1:3])

df_cartesian <- as.data.frame(wind)

true_obs <- df_cartesian[,4]


## Generate mesh for window slice

mesh  <- inla.mesh.2d(loc = as.matrix(loc.cartesian), max.edge = 0.005 )


## project mesh to lon lat coordinates

proj_ll <- inla.mesh.projector(mesh_fine, projection = "longlat", dims = c(2,2))

xy_ll <- expand.grid(proj_ll$x, proj_ll$y)

data_proj_ll <- as.vector(inla.mesh.project(proj_ll, field = as.vector(true_obs)))

## Here I receive error message:

##Fehler in projector$proj$A %*% as.vector(field) : 

## Cholmod-Fehler 'X and/or Y have wrong dimensions' bei Datei ##../MatrixOps/##cholmod_sdmult.c, Zeile 88


 I understand that it’s because the projection matrix A should have dimensions 

 4 X n_of_true_obs  but it has the dimensions 4 X mesh$n 

 I don’t know how to solve this problem, I couldn’t generate a mesh where 

mesh$n  = n_true_obs  

because mesh$n is always bigger or smaller than n_true_obs even if I work with a boundary definition. Also I would like to have a fine grid for precise inference.

##I would like to run the following could with the projection

truth_data_ll <- data.frame(lon = xy_ll[,1], lat = xy_ll[,2], field = data_proj_ll)

pl_truth_ll <- ggplot() +

  gg(truth_data_ll, mapping = aes_string("lon", "lat", fill = "field")) +

  coord_equal() +

  ggtitle("True field")


## this should produce something like this:



Any hint is welcome!

Regards,

Amelie Liese

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Problems plotting projected spherical data
parts:
The A-matrix should have dimension "number of evaluation
points"x"number of mesh points", since it's meant to be used to take a
function defined on a mesh and evaluate it one some other points (e.g.
a grid).
So it can help you to convert an inla-estimated spde model defined on
a mesh into values on a long-lat grid.
But I don't understand what you want to do to the true_obs values.
Perhaps you wanted to evaluate the estimated model (defined on a mesh)
at the locations where the true_obs are available? Then those
locations are what you need to provide to inla.mesh.projector().
If you provide them as a SpatialPoints object with correct CRS
information, I believe the internal project code will transform them
appropriately between that and the cartesian sphere coordinates (if
the mesh has a crs set to inla.CRS("sphere") I believe; see the
documentation for inla.CRS).

Finn
